This video explores 50 incredible geographic facts about Africa. 

These features:

Hemispheres and Global Position
Four Hemispheres: Africa is the only continent to span all four (0:32).
Eastern Alignment: Located centrally, it straddles the equator and prime meridian (5:57).
Continental Drift: The continent is moving northeast toward Europe (1:35).

Mountains and Volcanoes
Kilimanjaro: Africa's tallest mountain and a composite of three volcanic cones (2:55, 19:06).
Atlas Mountains: A major climate barrier between the Mediterranean and Sahara (5:19).
Drakensberg: Features towering cliffs and ancient rock art (14:03).

Deserts and Arid Regions
Sahara Desert: The world's largest hot desert (22:02), which was green 10,000 years ago (21:33).
Namib Desert: Famous for massive, iron-oxide-colored dunes meeting the Atlantic Ocean (12:16).
Sahel: The transitional zone facing severe desertification (13:10).
Salt Flats: Makgadikgadi Pan (Botswana) and Lake Assal (Djibouti) (7:59, 16:08).

Water Systems and Lakes
Nile River: The world’s longest river, flowing north (3:21, 21:06).
Congo River: The only river to cross the equator twice (4:15, 20:40).
Great Lakes: Contains massive amounts of freshwater, including Lake Tanganyika and Lake Malawi (7:00, 10:17).
Victoria Falls: The world’s largest waterfall by volume (7:30).
Okavango Delta: A unique seasonal oasis that peaks during the dry season (17:23).

Ecosystems and Resources
Congo Basin: The world's second-largest tropical rainforest, holding massive peat lands (11:20, 20:13).
Serengeti Migration: Annual loop of 1.5 million wildebeests (9:25).
Arable Land: Home to 60% of the world's uncultivated farmland (11:50).

Human and Geological History
Early Humans: Birthplace of the earliest stone tools (3:49) and home to human migration corridors (11:06).
Linguistic Diversity: Houses 30% of the world's languages (1:59).
Political Borders: 54 nations, largely drawn during the colonial era (15:15).
